title: Inverse image of a constant sheaf
statement:
For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ and a $\Lambda$-module (or
complex of $\Lambda$-modules) $M$, the canonical morphism
$f^{-1}\underline{M}\to\underline{M}$ is an isomorphism on
$X_{\Et}$.

proof.text: Write $c_{T,M}:M\to\underline M_T(T)$ for the constant-section map of the sheafification defining [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. For every etale $V\to Y$, send $m$ to its constant section on $V\times_YX$. These maps commute with restrictions and give a map of presheaves from the constant presheaf on $Y$ to $f_*\underline M_X$, using the direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] this factors uniquely through $\underline M_Y$. Its adjoint under [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is the canonical comparison $\alpha_M:f^{-1}\underline M_Y\to\underline M_X$. Every coefficient homomorphism $a:M\to N$ commutes with these maps, since both composites send $m$ to the constant section with value $a(m)$; uniqueness of sheafification and adjunction gives naturality of $\alpha_M$.

source.place: Tag 03Q0, definition-inverse-image (adjunction); construction from the universal property of constant-presheaf sheafification

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, and put $\bar y=f\circ\bar x$. The canonical pullback-stalk comparison [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies $(f^{-1}\underline M_Y)_{\bar x}$ with $(\underline M_Y)_{\bar y}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the constant-germ maps identify both $(\underline M_Y)_{\bar y}$ and $(\underline M_X)_{\bar x}$ with the underlying abelian group of $M$. Under these identifications $(\alpha_M)_{\bar x}$ sends $m$ to $m$: a representative constant section with value $m$ on $V$ pulls to the constant section with value $m$ on $V\times_YX$ and then restricts to any pointed neighbourhood mapping there. This is the germ description of the canonical comparison in Stacks 03Q1, not merely an abstract isomorphism between the two stalk groups. Since every germ is a constant germ by the cited constant-stalk theorem, the stalk map is the identity on all of $M$.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3) and equation-pullback; Tag 03PT, lemma-stalk-exact (2)

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the underlying abelian-sheaf map $\alpha_M$: step 2 proves it is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk. Thus it is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, apply step 1 naturality to the coefficient homomorphism $m\mapsto\lambda m$: this gives $\alpha_M\circ f^{-1}(\lambda)=\lambda\circ\alpha_M$. Thus the comparison respects constant scalars. For the module structure over the constant ring sheaf, a local scalar is locally represented by constants; the same equation holds on that cover, and equality follows by the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom. Its inverse also respects scalars: for a section $v$, write $u=\alpha_M^{-1}(v)$ and use $\alpha_M(\lambda u)=\lambda\alpha_M(u)=\lambda v$, so $\alpha_M^{-1}(\lambda v)=\lambda u$. Consequently $\alpha_M$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-module sheaves, without any finiteness, torsion, or invertibility assumption.

source.place: Tag 03PU, theorem-exactness-stalks; scalar compatibility from step 1 naturality and the sheaf axiom

proof.text: For a complex $M^\bullet$, use its termwise constant complex [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. In degree $r$ the comparison is $\alpha_{M^r}$. Naturality from step 1 applied to $d^r:M^r\to M^{r+1}$ says $\underline{d^r}_X\alpha_{M^r}=\alpha_{M^{r+1}}f^{-1}(\underline{d^r}_Y)$, so the comparisons form a chain map. Multiply this equation on the left by $\alpha_{M^{r+1}}^{-1}$ and on the right by $\alpha_{M^r}^{-1}$: $f^{-1}(\underline{d^r}_Y)\alpha_{M^r}^{-1}=\alpha_{M^{r+1}}^{-1}\underline{d^r}_X$. Thus the degreewise inverses from step 3 form its inverse chain map. This is an actual isomorphism of complexes, in every degree, and does not require boundedness.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: for a complex the same argument applies degreewise
